display.purpose: A name set as a title, in tracked capitals.

title.purpose: The titles of regions and dialogs.

nav.purpose: The name of a model in the navigator.

presentation.purpose: The heading of a presented step.

reading.purpose: The words of a presented step, in a column 64rem wide at most.

figure.purpose: The number of a presented step, in the display face.

technical.purpose: Identifiers, paths, versions, counts and times, in mono.

shadows.name: well
shadows.purpose: A field, a trough, a count cell or a pressed key: an inner shadow with a lit line along the foot.

shadows.name: sink
shadows.purpose: The well that a column's list lies in, cut as the picture cuts a container.

shadows.name: slab
shadows.purpose: A number that lies on a surface: a lit top edge, a 2px front edge and a short shadow.

shadows.name: edge-down
shadows.purpose: A header casting onto what is under it.

shadows.name: edge-side
shadows.purpose: A column casting onto what is beside it.

shadows.name: edge-up
shadows.purpose: A tray casting over the list that scrolls under it.

shadows.name: raised
shadows.purpose: A quiet key, a key cap, the voice circle or the chosen row of a list.

shadows.name: pressed
shadows.purpose: A raised control while pressed. The same value as well.

shadows.name: chosen
shadows.purpose: The chosen tab of a trough: the raised shadow and a 2px line of Gold Mark inside the foot.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Menus, tips, lists of matches, the floating sidebar and the voice box. The same value as card.

shadows.name: table
shadows.purpose: The tray that holds a plate. No shell surface uses it yet.

shadows.name: primary
shadows.purpose: The gold finish of a primary action at rest.

shadows.name: primary-hover
shadows.purpose: The gold finish under the pointer: a longer glow and a 2px contact line.

shadows.name: primary-pressed
shadows.purpose: The gold finish of a primary action while pressed.

motion.name: key
motion.purpose: The gold finish and the quiet key lift 1px under the pointer and sink 1px when pressed.

motion.name: presentation-box-in
motion.purpose: A presented walkthrough's column arrives once, moving 12px in from the side as it fades in (PRESENTATION_MS.boxIn).

motion.name: presentation-box-step
motion.purpose: A presented walkthrough's column hands one step to the next, with transform and opacity only (PRESENTATION_MS.boxStep). The wake of the rail settles last, at 1.3 times this pace.

narrative.overview:
The picture is a model in low relief that lies on a table. The shell is the furniture around it: rails, a header under the lamp, a tray at the foot of each column and a few pieces of gold hardware. An agent drew the picture, and the architect reads it. Nothing in the shell competes with the picture for attention, and nothing in the shell paints on it.

The shell is dense desktop chrome at 1920×1080. It uses 13px controls, 28px rows and small corners. Its neutrals are warm graphite and chalk, tinted toward the hue of the gold. Depth comes from planes, not from lines. The chrome stands on the picture and casts a short, warm, still shadow onto it. Controls stand on the chrome with a highlight on their top edge. Menus and dialogs float above everything. One warm yellow-gold marks what is chosen. It also marks the one primary action of a region, and that action is drawn as a physical piece of gold.

The shell speaks the language of the site's lit table. In its dark theme it shares the values of the site. In its light theme it translates them to chalk. A control is a physical key that lifts 1px under the pointer and sinks when it is pressed. A choice in a trough rises out of it as a raised face with a gold underline.
keyCharacteristics: The picture is the ground. The shell sits around it and over it.
Planes stack under a light from above. Each plane has a tone step, a highlight on its top edge and a warm shadow with an offset.
Keys are physical. A gold key and a quiet key lift on hover and sink on press, and a chosen tab rises out of its trough.
One gold has three uses: what is chosen, the one primary action, and the voice and the brand mark. On the picture, the palette's yellow is that gold, on purpose.
Tall condensed capitals set a name as a title. Plain sans sets every other word. Mono sets technical tokens only.
The shell is for the desktop only, near full screen at 1920×1080.

rules.name: The One Gold Rule
rules.body: Gold marks what is chosen, the one primary action of a region, and the voice and the brand mark. Nothing else in the shell is gold. On the picture there is one shared use, on purpose: the color named yellow in a vault's palette is the gold (`--semantic-yellow` is the gold mark, oklch(0.72 0.15 77) on chalk and oklch(0.86 0.125 86) on graphite), so a group, a kind or a relationship colored yellow is drawn in the gold. A yellow group's tab is drawn as a primary action is: the flat gold (`--primary`) with Gold Ink on it. The selection on the picture stays the only gold ring.

rules.name: The Ink On Chalk Rule
rules.body: Text on chalk is never gold. A gold dark enough to reach APCA Lc 60 on chalk reads as brown. Text stays in the ink, and a gold mark beside or under it carries the accent. On graphite, accent text is the gold itself (oklch(0.86 0.125 86)).

rules.name: The Untouched Picture Rule
rules.body: The renderer draws the picture. The shell never paints gold, shadow or decoration on a card in it.

rules.name: The One Ring Rule
rules.body: The gold ring goes round a card, a door, a frame or a relationship's label that is chosen. A line keeps its own ink, and the light says which lines stand.

rules.name: The Clear Tip Rule
rules.body: A reader rests on a part to read it and to see what it touches. So a tip stands against its part, on the nearest spot that leaves the part and what lights round it in view. On a dense picture it hides dim parts first, and it takes no pointer.

rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule
rules.body: Mono sets technical tokens only. It never sets a label or a heading.

rules.name: The Still Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow over the picture is a static box-shadow, and a panel's shadow never changes while the panel moves. No shell layer over the picture viewport uses backdrop-filter, filter or blur, and nothing there loops except the voice orb in the voice box, which is drawn on a canvas of its own and only while voice is on, and the warm wash the box takes from the orb's light, which is a layer of the box and never of the picture. A tip, a menu, the floating sidebar, the walkthrough box or the voice box may ease its own layer's transform and opacity, once, and each word of a subtitle may ease its own opacity, once. A select or a menu takes 160ms to arrive and 110ms to leave. The floating sidebar takes at most 160ms, the walkthrough box 220ms to arrive and 520ms to hand one step to the next, with the wake on its rail settling by about 700ms, and the voice box 360ms to arrive and 240ms to leave. A box that is wanted again while it leaves turns round from where it is. The orb itself crosses the page when subtitles are turned on or off, in a layer of its own, over 680ms.

rules.name: The Cursor Says What a Press Does Rule
rules.body: Whatever answers a click shows a pointer, in the shell and on the picture. A frame's floor is canvas, so it shows the arrow. Holding Space over the canvas shows an open hand, a press closes it, and a press with Space picks nothing.

rules.name: The Picture Answers Rule
rules.body: The light belongs to the picture, not to the shell. When a part or several parts are picked out, or the pointer rests on one, the viewer marks what stays as drawn, and the picture's own subjects recede far under an opacity filter, so that what stays is plainly on top. Several picks keep only themselves and the lines between them. The shell lays no layer, blur or halo over the picture to do it.

rules.name: The Card Is a Window Rule
rules.body: A card that opens a picture is a window onto it. The picture opens when the camera flies into the card, and going back flies out of it. The picture's picture sits inside the card, in the picture's own units, so one camera carries both and the picture that opens stands where the picture in the card stood. The picture blooms out of its middle as the camera flies in, and gathers again on the way back. The shell adds no layer for the flight.

rules.name: The Focus Pull Rule
rules.body: A move on the canvas is a rack of focus, and the painter draws it as part of the picture. What the reader goes to stays sharp. What they leave falls out of focus and sinks into the ground. A door stays sharp while the picture round it softens a little, and a picture comes into focus from its middle. A picture at rest is never soft, and a shell layer never blurs it. With reduced motion, or on the CPU painter, there is no blur.

rules.name: The Depth Rule
rules.body: A move between pictures shows where the next picture stands in the module tree. The modules nest, so a deeper picture lies inside this one and a shallower picture lies round it. A move to a picture at the same depth carries the reader sideways along a strip of pictures, in the order of the module tree. A move to a deeper picture zooms into it, and a move to a shallower picture zooms out to it. The camera flies through a card when the picture shows one on the way, and otherwise the two pictures zoom as one. The move never depends on the route: a card, a door, a crumb, the list and Back all take the same way. A view of one picture stays on that picture and has no way through the tree. With reduced motion, every move is a cut.

rules.name: The Spark Rule
rules.body: A picture's lines are drawn, and they never flash on together. A spark leaves each card that nothing feeds and runs along its lines. Where a spark lands, it runs both ways round the edge of the card and goes out, and the card's own lines start, so the picture builds along the way its parts talk. A label arrives as the spark reaches it. The cards land first, so the picture can be read while the lines run. A move between two pictures does the same for each line that changes its shape: the old line leaves, the cards settle on a clean ground, and a spark draws the new line. A line never swings across the picture, and a line that keeps its shape rides with its cards. A spark takes the line's color toward the text, so it stands out on both grounds. A traffic pulse stays light, because it travels on a line that already stands. With reduced motion, every line is there at once.

rules.name: The Planes Not Lines Rule
rules.body: Regions read as layered planes. A one-pixel rule stays only where it draws the edge of a control or a card, or where it divides regions on one plane.

rules.name: The Lit Plane Rule
rules.body: A raised plane carries a lit top edge, a contact line and a soft shadow, or it carries none. A contact line is 1px or 2px. No larger hard offset shadow appears in the shell.

rules.name: The Chosen Rises Rule
rules.body: In a trough, the chosen choice rises out of it as a Control Face in full ink with `shadow-chosen`. That shadow is the raised one with a 2px underline of Gold Mark inside the foot.

dos: Do draw the one primary action of a region with `primary-finish`, and only that one.
Do separate regions with tone steps and elevation tokens before you add a rule.
Do keep shadows warm and offset. Take them from the elevation tokens in app.css.
Do reach for `quiet-key`, `trough`, `chosen-face` and `plate` before you write a new shadow.
Do keep the ink on gold at Gold Ink (APCA Lc 66 or more).
donts: Do not put a shell layer with backdrop-filter, filter, blur or a looping animation over the picture viewport. The painter's focus is the picture's own, and it ends with the move.
Do not take a control out of a row when it cannot be used. Dim it and say why in its tooltip, so the row does not move.
Do not paint gold or decoration onto a card in the picture.
Do not use a grey-black blur or a halo without an offset as a shadow.
Do not add a phone or narrow layout.
Do not set a label or a heading in mono.
